$comment: DECLARED-UNDISPATCHED BALANCE ADAPTERS — read by UndispatchedAdapterGuard, enforced from IntegrationFromConfigBase._deployAllBalanceAdapters. The harness picks adapters out of deploy config by name and resolves each through a hand-maintained `_equals(name, ...)` chain in _deployBalanceAdapter, whose fall-through is `return address(0)`. Before this file existed, an adapter that was `enabled: true` in contracts-deployment-config but absent from that chain was skipped with a `[balanceAdapter] SKIP (unknown type):` console line and nothing else: not deployed, not registered on NAVCalculator, and never reached by _configureMetaInstances (which iterates DEPLOYED adapters, which is why a skipped meta-adapter does not trip the deliberately un-try/catch'd addMetaInstances call either). Note the asymmetry this fixes: the asset price-feed path in the same file already fails CLOSED on an unrecognised feed type (`revert("unknown price feed type ...")`); only the balance-adapter path failed open. THE HAZARD, which is worse than a missing test: an adapter that reports 0 because it was never deployed is indistinguishable from an account that holds nothing, so `script/test/refresh-integration-snapshot.sh` would regenerate `expected.<chainId>.navUsd8dp` from a computation that omits those positions and PIN THE UNDER-REPORT AS THE EXPECTED VALUE — silent, self-reinforcing, and thereafter defended by every subsequent run that agrees with it. That is latent only while the omitted positions are worth 0; the assisted family's caches are to be fed, at which point it stops being latent. THE RULE: every entry below must be an adapter that IS enabled in deploy config and IS skipped by the dispatch chain, and every such adapter must appear below with a non-empty reason. Both directions are enforced, so an undeclared skip fails the run AND a declaration that no longer corresponds to a real skip fails it too (a stale exemption cannot rot here). Adding a dispatch entry means deleting the matching line below in the same change. Keys are chainIds; adapter keys must not begin with '$'.
$assisted_family_note: The three `...Assisted` entries share one rationale, kept here rather than repeated per entry. They are the assisted balance-adapter family (ADR 0015 / ADR 0018): position coordinates are cached per account, amounts are always read live, and ownership is re-verified per read, so the family can only ever under-report. A non-zero balance in the harness therefore requires the coordinate cache to be seeded first. Seeding is trivial — the owner `submit`/`remove` are `msg.sender`-keyed (and the ADR 0030 keeper `submitFor` needs only a granted `SUBMITTER_ROLE`), so `vm.prank(account)` would do it with no Safe and no delegatecall — and that is precisely why a dispatch entry is NOT the right fix: a harness that seeds the cache it then reads asserts the VALUATION path works while leaving the delegatecall `BalanceAdapterAssistant` feeding path, where the family's under-report-only invariant actually lives, untested. Whether the integration suite should cover the feeding path at all, or leave it to the per-adapter assistant fork tests that already do, is a scoping decision and is deliberately open. WHERE THE COMPLETENESS GUARANTEE ACTUALLY LIVES, because it is not in this repository and a reader of `AssistedCoordCache` alone cannot see it: the cache is complete because the owner Safe's roles-modifier PERMISSION SET only permits the position-creating transactions via the assistant contracts — the direct path is not in the allow-list. That is an on-chain, auditable permission boundary, not process discipline. But it is enforced one layer UP, outside this repo: `AssistedCoordCache`'s owner mutators are `msg.sender`-keyed, the ADR 0030 keeper path only adds coverage, and the assistant is documented as the CANONICAL feeder rather than the only possible one, so do NOT infer the guarantee from this repo's contracts — follow it to the Safe's roles configuration. The residual risk is correspondingly narrow and is a SAFE-CONFIG REVIEW concern: if a change to the roles permission set ever adds a path that creates one of these positions WITHOUT going through the assistant, the cache silently misses it and the adapter under-reports, with no tripwire anywhere in this repo to catch it. That is what a reviewer of a roles change should watch for.

$attested_family_note: The `MerklRewards` entries share one rationale, kept here rather than repeated per chain. It is the attested balance-adapter family (ADR 0022): a per-(account, token) cache of a MERKLE-PROOF-VERIFIED amount, which reads 0 whenever the cached root differs from the live Distributor root, so — like the assisted family — it can only ever under-report. A non-zero balance in the harness therefore requires the cache to be fed first, and unlike the assisted family that is NOT trivial to fake: submits are gated on SUBMITTER_ROLE, and the payload must carry a merkle proof that verifies against the live root at the fork block. A harness that granted itself the role and submitted a proof it constructed would assert the VALUATION path while leaving the proof-verification path — where this family's integrity actually lives — tested only where it already is, in the adapter's own fork tests against the real Distributor root. That is why this is a declared skip rather than a dispatch entry. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WITH PRODUCTION: on-chain the cache is fed by an off-chain keeper holding SUBMITTER_ROLE, so until that keeper is deployed and granted the role, the LIVE adapter also reports 0 — the harness and production agree today, and both under-report by exactly the unclaimed Merkl rewards. REVISIT BEFORE THE NEXT SNAPSHOT REFRESH once the keeper is running: while the adapter reports 0 the omission is invisible, and a refresh run in that state would pin the under-report as the expected NAV. No fixture exercises this today — `merkl` appears nowhere in test/integration/accounts.json, neither as a cached DeBank item nor in any chain's supportedDeBankProtocols — so there is no known omitted value at present, only a latent one.
